items.item: Correspondent bank and receiving bank charges
items.reason: The BOC and HSBC pages publish only the sending bank's fee. No official schedule for the intermediary or the US receiving bank was found.
items.action: Read a real remittance advice: the difference between the amount sent and the amount credited is the true charge. Alternatively ask each bank in writing.

items.item: Wise fee and FX spread for CNY to USD
items.reason: The Wise help page read describes eligibility, per-transfer limits and the overall limit, but publishes no fee for this corridor.
items.action: Open a Wise quote for a CNY transfer and record the mid-market rate, the applied rate and the fee.

items.item: UnionPay card FX fee and conversion spread
items.reason: No official UnionPay or issuing-bank page stating the card FX fee was available for this section.
items.action: Ask the issuing bank for the card's overseas transaction and ATM fee schedule in writing; compare one foreign transaction against the board rate on the same day.

items.reason: The tariff PDF header carries two dates (31 Oct 2026 and 2024-09-12), so the version in force is not unambiguous from the page read.
items.action: Confirm with HSBC China which version applies to an outward remittance executed today.

items.item: Conversion rate actually applied to HSBC Global Transfer
items.reason: The tariff prices the transfer but does not state which rate converts CNY to USD. The model applies the published board spread, which is a stated assumption, not a published price for the product.
items.action: Execute a small Global Transfer and read the rate on the confirmation; substitute it into model.py.

items.item: HSBC Advance Global Transfer charge: CNY 145 or USD 20
items.reason: The tariff shows CNY 145 with the note that the actual charge is USD 20 or equivalent. The model uses USD 20.
items.action: Read the debit line on a completed Advance transfer.

items.item: HSBC Premier monthly fee excluded from the M03 cost rows
items.reason: Premier costs CNY 300 per month unless total relationship balance is at least CNY 500,000. It is a relationship fee, not a transfer fee, so it is excluded from cost-per-transfer rather than added arbitrarily to every row.
items.action: If your balance stays below CNY 500,000 for the months you use this route, add CNY 300 per month to the M03 figure.

items.reason: No official page read states how much RMB cash an individual may carry out of China. The route is therefore left unpriced rather than estimated.
items.action: Read the current 携带人民币现钞出入境 notice on the PBOC or customs site and add it to the ledger before using the route.

items.reason: The article is cited by two SAFE Tianjin pages, but the circular itself was not opened for this section, so its wording is not quoted anywhere here.
items.action: Open the circular on safe.gov.cn and add its text to the ledger if the exact wording of Article 59 matters.

items.item: Business income and equity proceeds conversion route
items.reason: The service guide lists documents for business income and for capital gains, but no separate price or processing route was found for those categories.
items.action: Ask the local SAFE branch which item code applies to business income from a sole proprietorship or equity sale.

items.reason: The IRS page states that penalties may apply under IRC 6039F(c) but does not state the amount on the page read.
items.action: Read the Form 3520 instructions for the current penalty formula before relying on a figure.

items.item: Settlement time for each bank route
items.reason: Neither the BOC fee page nor the HSBC tariff states the credit time for an individual outward remittance.
items.action: Record the send and credit timestamps on a test transfer.

items.item: Tax actually payable on the section 988 gain
items.reason: The gain is ordinary income; the tax depends on your bracket and other income, which are not known. The site publishes the gain percentage and the formula, not a tax figure.
items.action: Apply your marginal rate to the computed gain, or run Form 1040 Schedule D and the section 988 worksheet.

items.item: Board dates are one day apart
items.reason: BOC is timestamped 2026-11-11 20:39 and HSBC 2026-11-10, so the two spreads are not measured at the same instant. The ranking (BOC spread is roughly half the HSBC spread) is far larger than a one-day move.
items.action: Re-run model.py with both boards read on the same day.

items.reason: PBOC Announcement [2004] No.16 covers both emigrant and inheritance transfers, but the provincial service guide read covers only the emigrant item, so the inheritance procedure and its approval threshold were not priced.
items.action: Find the inheritance (继承财产转移) service item on a provincial SAFE site and read its conditions.

items.item: Bank discretion above the annual quota
items.reason: SAFE rules require documents but do not publish a decision time or an approval probability for documented purchases beyond the quota.
items.action: Ask the branch in writing before committing to a date, and keep the reply.

items.item: Card spending is not a conversion route
items.reason: Route M06 is included because it is commonly proposed, but it converts consumption rather than the balance, and its annual cap is about USD 15,000 at the board rate.
items.action: Treat M06 as a spending channel, not a repatriation route.
